abstract: A published claim reports that RL post-training turns a 4B language model into a cheaper supply-chain agent than the same model untrained. We test a claim of that type at four sizes (0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B) under a pre-registered paired cost criterion, with matched untrained controls. Post-training does help at 4B: 9,346 against 21,578 at seed 0 (30/30 paired wins) and 17,958 at seed 1 (25/30, marginal at the criterion's bar). It does not help at 0.6B, where six trained rows lose; it makes 1.7B worse on every seed (27,706 to 94,887 against 11,508); and at 8B one arm of four passes (14,594 against 89,633). The result that survives all of it is simpler: no arm at any size beats the reference we actually care about. A self-tuning order-up-to rule costs 5,346 in the same simulator and horizon. The closest arm is 1.75x that at its best seed and 3.36x at its other seed; the worst is 17.7x. Scale did not close the gap.
